claims.text: The recovered source asks for spiral output of an existing matrix; it does not specify the concrete direction, start corner, API or matrix-generation task.
After emitting each current outer edge and shrinking its boundary, the remaining unvisited cells form the smaller rectangle; re-checking row/column bounds prevents duplicates in degenerate layers.
The traversal emits each matrix element exactly once, requiring O(m*n) time and O(1) algorithmic auxiliary state beyond the output list.
The exact Java implementation passes 15 fixed checks and 5000 deterministic randomized matrix comparisons against an independent visited-direction-walk oracle while preserving the input matrix.

checks: rectangular traversal in the candidate's clockwise top-left contract
single-row, single-column and rectangular layer closure
5000 deterministic random matrices checked against an independently structured oracle

boundary_tests.expected: each element appears exactly once without duplicate closing edges

boundary_tests.expected: boundary shrinking preserves exact clockwise order
element values do not affect coordinate traversal
